finding: Main web responses lack CSP/frame-ancestors and several browser isolation headers
verification: 2026-09-24 (ct-54096): packages/web/server/responsePolicy.ts. LIVE on the next web deploy: Strict-Transport-Security max-age=86400 (no includeSubDomains, no preload; http://codecast.sh 301s to https, checked 2026-09-23). REPORT-ONLY: the full draft document policy (DOCUMENT_POLICY; sources and reasons in plans/security-csp-draft.md), reporting to Sentry's CSP security endpoint derived from VITE_SENTRY_DSN (a Railway runtime variable), only on Railway, for 10% of HTML documents, capped at 120 reporting documents per hour per process, via report-uri plus report-to and Reporting-Endpoints. Nothing is enforced: no Content-Security-Policy header is sent.

Tests: packages/web/server/responsePolicy.test.ts 8 pass through the Hono middleware (DSN to endpoint, sampling, hourly cap, no DSN, HSTS, draft sources, no enforcing header); server shareMeta and staticAssets suites pass; cast check web clean.

Browser: the local server on the built dist (port 3977) boots and renders in Chrome with the headers; every loaded origin is in the draft. The signed-in prod app (read-only check in the founder's Chrome) loaded 12 origins, all covered: Convex img/fetch/iframe, GitHub, Slack and Gravatar avatars, Google Fonts. Not exercised with a signed-in local origin (no real accounts): calls, OAuth return, desktop windows. The header is report-only, so it cannot block them.
REVIEW on or after 2026-10-08: read the Sentry CSP reports, then fix inline scripts (hash or nonce) and decide on enforcement, and whether to raise HSTS to one year.
